To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) there are wide variations in the coverage levels and trends of access to water supply, sanitation, and hygiene in the 31 major cities of Sub-Saharan Africa, 2) most of the cities have made progress towards the Millennium Development Goals in terms of improved access to improved water supply and sanitation, but 3) fewer than half have reduced the amount of time people spend collecting water, and 4), on average, open defecation is becoming more common.

the majority of the cities in the study were increasing access to improved water supply and sanitation, while fewer cities made progress in reducing the time spent collecting and in reducing open defacation.
there is wide variability in access to WS &S among the 31 cities in SSA.
